business-e2e-context · Bunkai TMS

Business E2E map

Built 2026-10-12 from upex-bunkai-tms origin/staging 98ee1b4 (2026-10-11), the live database through the read-only QA role and the OpenAPI contract. Journeys first, then the feature catalog they cross. Every fact a figure shows is also in the text.

Overview

Who uses Bunkai. Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System. People work inside a workspace with one of four roles the database recognizes: viewer, member, admin, owner (workspace_members.role). The same person can hold different roles in different workspaces; the browser works on one active workspace at a time (a cookie set from the sidebar switcher, POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace). Besides people in a browser, programmatic callers (CLI, CI, AI agents) use a personal access token (bk_pat_…) that acts as its owner and is limited by scopes. Three system actors act without a person: the run inactivity sweep and the workspace purge (pg_cron), and the daily digest (Vercel Cron).

Role hierarchy. viewer (read only), then member (does all QA work), then admin (adds team management and the billing overview), then owner (adds billing checkout, data export, workspace deletion and restore). The owner role is never granted by an invite.

The interface hides most write controls from viewers, but not all of them: the New ATC and New Test buttons and the ATC editor's save are shown to every role and the server refuses the write (see persona-viewer).

Surfaces

Signed-out pages: /login, /invites/accept, /workspaces/{id}/restore, and the public explainers /about (guided tour, Spanish), /qa (testability guide for QA) and /api/docs (API reference). Signed-in, a global sidebar (Home, Activity, Projects, Settings, notification bell, command palette) frames everything; inside a project a persistent workbench (explorer tree, tabs, toolbar) carries a project sub-nav: All ATCs, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Traceability, Milestones, Test Plans. The middleware sends a signed-out visitor of /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings or /activity to /login?next=….

The journeys that carry the product, by business risk

  1. Execute a Test and file bugs (journey-execute-test-run, journey-file-and-triage-bug): the execution evidence and defects are the product's output; a wrong verdict or a lost bug defeats its purpose.
  2. Author an ATC anchored to its story (journey-author-atc): enforced traceability is the value proposition; an ATC that escapes its story and criteria breaks every report.
  3. Sign in and create the first workspace (journey-sign-in-and-onboarding): the activation funnel; nothing else is reachable without it.
  4. Join a team by invite and keep tenants apart (journey-join-workspace-by-invite, cross-feature-active-workspace): cross-tenant leakage is the top security risk.
  5. Review quality (journey-review-quality): coverage, traceability and run reports are what a lead decides on.
  6. Upgrade to Cloud (journey-upgrade-to-cloud): the only place money changes hands.
  7. Delete, restore or export a workspace (journey-delete-and-restore-workspace, journey-export-workspace-data): irreversible after 30 days; blast radius is the whole tenant.

Usage in the shared database (read-only QA role, 2026-10-12). Active memberships: 1,074 owner, 17 member, 8 admin, 8 viewer; 19 workspaces have more than one member. Runs by executor: 1,276 human, 48 agent, 26 ci. Most rows are QA and automation test data, so these numbers show what is exercised, not real customer behaviour.

Persona: QA member

System role. member (default role of an invite). Evidence: workspace_members.role in supabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql; write gate membership.role !== 'viewer' in app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/layout.tsx.

Goals. Turn requirements into verifiable checks and evidence: build the module tree and stories (or import them from Jira), author ATCs anchored to acceptance criteria, chain them into Tests, run Tests against an environment, file bugs from failed steps and move bugs through triage.

Pain points the code makes visible (quoted messages):

  • "An ATC needs a User Story and at least one Acceptance Criterion." and "Pick a Module for this ATC." (lib/atcs/builder-guards.ts)
  • "At least one step is required." (lib/atcs/builder-guards.ts)
  • "No environments configured" next to the Start run control when the project has no environment (components/tests/StartRunButton.tsx); 1,736 of 1,866 projects have none (data map flow-environments).
  • "Please give a reason of at least 3 characters" when aborting a run (components/runs/RunnerView.tsx).
  • A 409 when someone else saved the same ATC first (optimistic version lock, data map flow-author-atc).

Permissions. Row "member" of the matrix in overview: everything except team management, billing, export and deletion.

Test account. The QA repo declares one pair per environment, STAGING_USER_EMAIL / LOCAL_USER_EMAIL (.env.example); the role that user holds is not recorded. A dedicated member account is needed (for example STAGING_MEMBER_EMAIL, to be created).

Journeys. journey-build-project-structure, journey-author-atc, journey-compose-test, journey-execute-test-run, journey-file-and-triage-bug, journey-plan-testing, journey-review-quality, journey-join-workspace-by-invite.

Persona: viewer (stakeholder)

System role. viewer. Evidence: invite role options in app/(app)/workspaces/[id]/members/members-client.tsx; every write gate in the UI is role !== 'viewer'.

Goals. Follow quality without changing it: browse the ATC library, Tests, run reports, bugs, metrics, traceability and the activity feed; receive nothing by assignment (a viewer cannot be a bug assignee, 45313).

Pain points. The project toolbar shows "New ATC" and "New Test" to every role (project-shell.tsx), and the New ATC and New Test pages have no role check (atcs/new/page.tsx, tests/new/page.tsx); the ATC editor's save is a server action with no role check of its own (atcs/[atcId]/actions.ts). The write is refused by the database, so a viewer can fill a form and only learn at save time.

Permissions. Read everything in the workspace, leave it; nothing else.

Test account. None declared; needs one (for example STAGING_VIEWER_EMAIL, to be created).

Journeys. journey-review-quality, journey-join-workspace-by-invite.

Persona: workspace admin (QA lead)

System role. admin. Evidence: BILLING_NAV_ROLES = ['owner', 'admin'] in lib/settings/nav-items.ts; invite RLS (data map flow-invite-and-membership).

Goals. Grow and shape the team (invite by email with role viewer, member or admin; rotate or revoke a link), watch plan usage on the billing overview, and do all member work. Can issue tokens carrying workspace:admin.

Pain points. Bunkai sends no invite email: the admin gets "Invite link for {email} copied to clipboard." and must deliver it (members-client.tsx). The Members page /workspaces/{id}/members has no link anywhere in the running UI: its only link lives in components/layout/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx, which nothing renders, and Settings lists "Members" as coming soon. An admin reaches it only by typing the URL.

Permissions. Member rights plus invites and the billing overview; not checkout, export or deletion.

Test account. None declared; needs one (for example STAGING_ADMIN_EMAIL, the example name the QA repo's .env.schema comment uses).

Journeys. journey-join-workspace-by-invite (issuing side), journey-review-quality, plus every member journey.

Persona: workspace owner (buyer)

System role. owner, created by bunkai_bootstrap_workspace when a user creates a workspace (supabase/migrations/0006_bootstrap_workspace.sql). A workspace can have several owners.

Goals. Create the workspace, pay for Cloud seats, take the data out, and end the workspace (delete, with a 30-day restore window).

Pain points. "Slug "{slug}" is taken — try another." on workspace creation (onboarding-form.tsx); a type-the-name confirmation before deletion (DeleteWorkspaceModal.tsx); the last owner cannot leave (isSoleOwner in lib/account/workspaces.ts).

Permissions. Everything in the matrix.

Test account. The self-signed-up user of any test account is an owner of the workspace it creates; whether STAGING_USER_EMAIL is that user was not verified.

Journeys. journey-sign-in-and-onboarding, journey-upgrade-to-cloud, journey-export-workspace-data, journey-delete-and-restore-workspace, plus every admin and member journey.

Persona: automation client (AI agent, CI, CLI)

System role. Not a role: a personal access token acting as its owner, so the owner's workspace role still applies, narrowed by the token's scopes atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin (lib/api/pat.ts). On POST /api/v1/runs a token caller may declare executor_mode human, agent or ci; a browser caller is always human (app/api/v1/runs/route.ts).

Goals. Create and execute Tests headlessly: sign in by API (/auth/signin returns a token), read and write ATCs, start runs, mark steps, finish them, file bugs.

Pain points. Nine routes are cookie-only and answer 403 to a token: token issue and revoke, active workspace, leave, data export and download, workspace delete and restore (data map discovery-gaps, app/qa/qa-config.ts). A token's raw value is shown once.

Token issue in the UI. Settings, Tokens: name, at least one scope, expiry 30, 90 (default) or 365 days or never, optional workspace binding (components/settings/IssueTokenModal.tsx).

Test account. Same user pair as the browser; the QA repo mints its token through bun run api:login (package.json).

Usage. 48 agent and 26 ci runs in the shared database; 8,943 non-revoked tokens (data map state-access-token).

Journeys. journey-automate-via-api.

Journey: sign in and create the first workspace

Persona. Any new or returning user; the creator becomes owner. Entry. / (redirects to /home or /login, app/page.tsx), any protected URL (middleware adds ?next=), or an emailed magic link.

  1. Enter email; the form calls POST /api/v1/auth/check-email and branches on whether the account exists (app/(auth)/login/email-first-form.tsx).
  2. Existing account: enter password, POST /api/v1/auth/signin. An unconfirmed account is routed to the code step with "Verify your email with the code we sent before signing in."
  3. New account: password of at least 8 characters, POST /api/v1/auth/signup; then enter the emailed code (6 to 8 digits) at POST /api/v1/auth/confirm; "Resend" calls POST /api/v1/auth/resend.
  4. On success the browser goes to next (only same-site paths starting with one slash; default /projects, lib/urls.ts).
  5. /projects and /home send a user with no active membership to /onboarding; a user who already has one is bounced from /onboarding back to /projects (app/(app)/onboarding/page.tsx).
  6. Create workspace: name plus a slug of 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, POST /api/v1/workspaces; success replaces the page with /projects.

Alternative entries

  • Magic link (POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link), then /auth/callback verifies it; an invalid link lands on /login?error=magic_link_invalid.
  • GitHub or Google OAuth (/auth/oauth/[provider]), back through /auth/callback; failures land on /login?error=oauth_init_failed or otp_exchange_failed.

Branches and failure points

  • Wrong password: "That email or password is incorrect." Existing email on sign-up: "An account already exists for this email. Try signing in instead."
  • Bad code: "That code is invalid or expired." Rate limit on any step: "Too many attempts. Please wait a moment and retry."
  • Slug collision: "Slug "{slug}" is taken — try another." Invalid slug: "Use at least 3 letters or digits — they become the URL slug."
  • External-dependency steps: the emailed code, the magic link and the OAuth consent screen need a mailbox or a provider account the test session cannot produce; they are not automatable as written.

Where data changes hands. Account creation in Supabase Auth; workspace plus owner membership in one transaction; the headless sign-in and confirm calls also mint a token. Data: business-data-context flow-sign-in-and-onboarding.

Journey: join a team by invite

Personas. Admin or owner (issues), any invitee (accepts). Entry. The admin opens /workspaces/{id}/members (by URL; see persona-admin); the invitee opens the accept link the admin sent outside Bunkai.

  1. Admin enters an email and a role (viewer, member or admin), POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites; the accept link is copied to the clipboard.
  2. Admin may "Rotate link" or "Revoke" a pending invite from the same page.
  3. Invitee opens /invites/accept?token=…; when signed out the page sends them to /login?next=… and back.
  4. Signed in with the invited email, the page posts the token to POST /api/v1/invites/accept; "Welcome — you have joined the workspace."
  5. The invitee switches to the new workspace from the sidebar switcher (POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace).

Branches and failure points

  • Revoked, already accepted or expired (7 days) invite: 409 with a specific message; a deleted workspace's invite answers like an unknown token.
  • Signed in with a different email: refused (email must match).
  • Inviting someone who is already an active member: refused. Seat limits are not checked.
  • Silent failure point: the link is never emailed, so an invite the admin forgets to deliver simply expires (64 of 117 invites in the shared database expired).

Data: business-data-context flow-invite-and-membership, state-invite.

Journey: build the project structure

Persona. Member and above. Entry. Sidebar "+" next to Projects (/projects/new) or an existing project from /projects.

  1. Create a project (name 3 to 80 characters with at least one letter or digit; description up to 5 KB), POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/projects.
  2. In the workbench explorer, add a root module, then use a module's menu: New sub-module, New user story, Rename, Move, Delete (components/layout/Sidebar.tsx). Module description up to 500 characters.
  3. Add a user story to a module (title, description, optional Jira key), POST /api/v1/modules/{id}/user-stories.
  4. Story menu, Manage criteria: add, reorder, edit and remove acceptance criteria, and set the story to ready to test (acceptance-criteria-panel.tsx).
  5. Or import: "Import" in the explorer header opens the Jira dialog (a JQL query), POST /api/v1/imports; the dialog polls GET /api/v1/imports/{id} until the job completes.

Branches and failure points

  • Project name taken: "A project with this name already exists here."; reserved name: "This name is reserved. Try a different one." The plan's project limit (Community 3) is enforced by a database trigger; the message the form shows for it was not verified.
  • Module move into its own subtree or beyond depth 6: refused. Delete on a module, story or criterion archives the whole subtree, including its ATCs.
  • Ready to test without any active criterion: refused (45010); archiving the last criterion drops the story back to draft.
  • A second import on the same project while one runs: 409. A Jira authentication failure fails the whole job; external dependency on the platform's Jira account.

Data: business-data-context flow-author-structure, flow-jira-import, entity-module.

Journey: author an ATC

Persona. Member and above. Entry. "New ATC" in the project toolbar, or a story's tree entry (/atcs/new?story={id}, also with &ac={id}), which preselects the story and module.

  1. Pick the module, the user story and at least one of that story's acceptance criteria (anchoring panel).
  2. Write the title (3 to 200 characters), steps in Markdown and assertions in YAML, choose the layer (UI, API, Unit), optional technique and priority, up to 10 tags; a live preview renders the result.
  3. Save: POST /api/v1/atcs; "ATC created" and the page opens /projects/{slug}/atcs/{id}.
  4. Edit later from the ATC page; save runs a server action that calls bunkai_update_atc and reports how many Tests use the ATC (those Tests change on their next read).
  5. Duplicate from the ATC's explorer menu (POST /api/v1/atcs/{id}/duplicate).

Branches and failure points

  • Client guards before save: "Pick a Module for this ATC.", "An ATC needs a User Story and at least one Acceptance Criterion.", "Title must be between 3 and 200 characters.", "At least one step is required.", "An ATC can have at most 10 tags."
  • Server refusals: criterion outside the story (45020), module outside the project (45021), stale version on edit (45022, someone saved first).
  • The edit path sends no expected version from the UI (ifMatch: null in actions.ts); whether the browser editor can lose a concurrent edit silently was not verified.
  • There is no delete: an ATC leaves the library only when its module subtree is archived.

Data: business-data-context flow-author-atc, entity-atc.

Journey: compose a Test

Persona. Member and above (reorder and Start run are hidden from viewers). Entry. "New Test" in the project toolbar; existing Tests are listed in the explorer's Tests group.

  1. Give the Test a title (1 to 200 characters) and pick ATCs into an ordered chain (the same ATC may appear more than once), POST /api/v1/tests; "Test created".
  2. On the Test page (tabs Steps and Run History), drag to reorder the chain (PATCH /api/v1/tests/{id}/reorder) and edit suite tags (PUT /api/v1/tests/{id}/tags; smoke, sanity, regression are reserved and lower-cased).
  3. Filter the explorer's Tests by tag (GET /api/v1/tests?tag=…).

Branches and failure points

  • Empty chain (45120), bad title (45121), an ATC from another workspace (45122): refused.
  • Reorder or tag edit against a stale version: refused (version guard).
  • Silent surprise: Tests belong to the workspace, not the project, so every project's explorer lists all Tests of the workspace (app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/layout.tsx selects by workspace_id).

Data: business-data-context flow-compose-test-and-plan, entity-test.

Journey: execute a Test (run)

Persona. Member and above in the browser; the automation client through the API (journey-automate-via-api). Entry. A Test page (/projects/{slug}/tests/{id}).

  1. If the project has no environment, add one from the explorer's Environments group (name 1 to 50 characters, unique per project ignoring case); otherwise the Start run control reads "No environments configured".
  2. Pick an environment and press "Start run": POST /api/v1/runs with an Idempotency-Key header; "Run started" and the runner opens at /projects/{slug}/runs/{runId}.
  3. Mark each step passed, failed or blocked, with an optional note and evidence URL (POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark); "Step marked". A step can be re-marked while the run is running; the last mark wins.
  4. On any failed step, "Report bug" opens the bug dialog prefilled from the step (default severity P3); see journey-file-and-triage-bug.
  5. Close: "Finish run" with a verdict passed or failed (the person chooses it; it is not computed), or "Abort" with a reason of 3 to 500 characters. Pending steps become skipped.

Branches and failure points

  • Environment of another project (45201) or a chain with no executable step (45202): refused at start.
  • Two people close the same run: the first wins, the other gets 409 and the server message is shown verbatim.
  • Marks arrive live in other open browsers through Supabase Realtime (run_atcs, run_steps); the run header itself is not pushed, so a run closed elsewhere may look open until reload (not verified in a browser).
  • Silent failure: a run left open is aborted by the inactivity sweep after 4 hours with no mark (1,157 of 1,192 aborted runs in the shared database), and the starter is notified.
  • Viewers see the run read-only: no mark, finish, abort or Report bug (canManageRun).

Where data changes hands. Start copies the Test's chain into an immutable run snapshot; every mark writes a step result and recomputes the ATC verdict. Data: business-data-context flow-execute-run, state-run, state-run-step.

Journey: file and triage a bug

Persona. Member and above (the list is read-only for viewers). Entry. "Report bug" on a failed run step, or "New bug" on Bug Reports (/projects/{slug}/bugs) for a standalone bug.

  1. Fill title (5 to 200 characters), severity P1 to P4, description, steps to reproduce and up to 10 evidence URLs; POST /api/v1/bugs; "Bug filed". A run-linked bug carries the run, step and ATC; a standalone one shows "Filed manually".
  2. From the list, assign or reassign to an active non-viewer member (POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/assign).
  3. Advance the status one stage: open, in progress, resolved, closed (POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/status).
  4. The new assignee, and on status changes the reporter and assignee, get an inbox notification; unread ones go out in the daily email digest.
  5. Open a bug (/bugs/{bugId}) to see its origin: run, failed step position, ATC title and layer; a run page shows its linked bug and scrolls to the failing step.

Branches and failure points

  • Skipping a stage (45310) or going backward or reopening (45311): refused; a closed bug cannot be reopened.
  • Assignee who is not an active member (45312) or is a viewer (45313): refused.
  • A module archived after filing: the bug stays and is tagged "Archived"; the project list excludes archived modules.
  • Silent point: filing and unassigning notify nobody; the person who changes the status is never notified of their own change.

Usage: 12 bugs filed from a run step and 1,743 standalone in the shared database. Data: business-data-context flow-file-and-triage-bug, state-bug, flow-notifications.

Journey: plan testing with test plans and milestones

Persona. Member and above (viewers read). Entry. Project sub-nav "Test Plans" and "Milestones".

  1. Create a test plan: name 1 to 100 characters (unique per project ignoring case), goal up to 100, description up to 500; POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/test-plans.
  2. Open the plan and add Tests through the picker (search, POST /api/v1/test-plans/{id}/tests); remove one from the table (membership only).
  3. Create a milestone with a name and a target date from today up to 5 years ahead; edit it later.

Branches and failure points

  • A Test whose chain reaches outside the plan's project: refused (45604).
  • Plans are editable only while open, and nothing in the UI or API closes a plan; 5 plans in the database are closed anyway (origin not verified).
  • Milestones link to nothing: no plan, run or bug references them, so a milestone is a dated label only.

Data: business-data-context flow-compose-test-and-plan, state-test-plan.

Journey: review quality

Personas. Any role, viewer included (all reports are read-only). Entry. /home (the landing route after sign-in from /).

  1. Home: welcome banner, recent projects, active runs, open bugs by severity (open plus in progress), workspace coverage summary, recent activity.
  2. Project Metrics: coverage per acceptance criterion and per module (uncovered, not run, executed), plus recovery cycles per story.
  3. Traceability: pick a user story; see its chain criterion to ATC to Test to Run to Bug (also reachable with ?story={id}).
  4. Test Runs: the project's runs filtered by status, executor, module and start date with pass and fail totals; a Test's Run History tab filters one Test's runs by outcome.
  5. Bug Reports: list plus a defect heatmap per module over 7, 30 or 90 days with a week-over-week trend.
  6. Activity: the workspace audit feed. Command palette (sidebar search): ATCs, Tests, projects, modules, bugs and runs in one search.

Branches and failure points

  • A project the caller cannot see answers not found (no existence signal).
  • A failed ATC still counts as covered; an ATC whose last run was skipped or blocked counts as not run (data map flow-reports). A reader who expects "coverage = passing" misreads the KPI.
  • The global sidebar entries ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports and Metrics are disabled ("Coming soon"): workspace-wide views do not exist; the project-scoped ones are in the sub-nav.

Data: business-data-context flow-reports.

Journey: automate through the API

Persona. Automation client, set up by a member or above. Entry. Settings, Tokens, or headless sign-in.

  1. Get a token: in the browser, "Issue token" (name, scopes, expiry, optional workspace) shows the raw value once; headless, POST /api/v1/auth/signin or /auth/confirm returns one.
  2. Read the contract at /api/docs (rendered from /api/openapi, 102 operations) and the public testability guide at /qa.
  3. Call the same endpoints the UI calls with Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_…: author ATCs (atc:write), create Tests, start runs with executor_mode agent or ci (run:execute), mark, finish, file bugs.
  4. Revoke from Settings, Tokens (browser only).

Branches and failure points

  • Missing scope: refused. Expired or revoked token: uniform 401.
  • Cookie-only routes answer 403 to a token (see persona-automation-client).
  • POST /api/v1/runs without an Idempotency-Key header: refused ("Missing Idempotency-Key header."); the same key with a different body: "Idempotency-Key reused with a different request payload." (lib/api/idempotency.ts).
  • Leaving or deleting a workspace revokes that workspace's tokens; a pipeline silently starts failing with 401.

Data: business-data-context entity-access-token, state-access-token.

Journey: upgrade to the Cloud plan

Persona. Owner (admins see the overview only). Entry. Settings, Billing.

  1. Billing overview: plan, purchased and active seats, project count, oldest run age.
  2. Open the upgrade page; compare Community, Cloud and Enterprise; choose a seat quantity (Cloud 24.00 USD per seat).
  3. Start checkout, POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout; the browser goes to Stripe's hosted page. Money changes hands here, outside Bunkai.
  4. Paid: Stripe returns to /settings/billing?upgraded=1, which polls the overview until the plan reads Cloud; the plan changes only when Stripe's webhook reports the payment as paid.
  5. Canceled on Stripe: return to the upgrade page with ?checkout=canceled; "Checkout canceled. Nothing was charged." and the session is expired.

Branches and failure points

  • Seat quantity out of range: "Seat quantity must be a whole number between {min} and {max}."
  • A second checkout while one is open: refused (one open session per workspace).
  • External-dependency step: Stripe's hosted payment page; in tests it needs Stripe test mode, which is not verified for staging.
  • Silent point: the return page can show the old plan until the webhook lands; a delayed or failed async payment leaves the plan unchanged.
  • No downgrade, cancellation or renewal handling exists.

Usage: 7 checkout sessions, all expired; no workspace is on Cloud. Data: business-data-context flow-billing-upgrade.

Journey: export workspace data

Persona. Owner, browser session only. Entry. Settings, Data export (hidden from other roles).

  1. Request an export, POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/data-export; the page shows the job queued, then running.
  2. A background worker builds a zip of projects, modules, stories, criteria, ATCs, Tests, runs, bugs, activity and memberships.
  3. When completed, download it (GET …/data-export/download) within 168 hours.

Branches and failure points

  • A second request while one is active: 409. Expired archive: download refused.
  • Silent failure: if the background worker never runs, the job stays queued and nothing retries it.

Usage: 5 export jobs in the shared database. Data: business-data-context flow-workspace-export.

Journey: leave, delete or restore a workspace

Personas. Any member (leave), owner (delete, restore). Entry. Settings, Workspaces.

  1. Leave: type the workspace name to confirm, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/membership; that workspace's tokens are revoked.
  2. Delete (owner): type the name, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}; "{name} was deleted." Access ends for everyone at once; tokens and pending invites are revoked; every active member gets an email with a restore link.
  3. Restore within 30 days: the owner opens /workspaces/{id}/restore (signed out, it goes through login), POST …/restore; "Workspace restored."
  4. After 30 days the daily purge deletes the workspace and everything in it.

Branches and failure points

  • Leaving the caller's only workspace, or as the last owner: refused.
  • Restore by a non-owner or of a live workspace: refused. Restored workspaces keep their tokens and invites revoked.
  • Silent point: the restore email depends on Resend; if it fails the deletion still happens and the owner must find the restore URL another way.
  • Irreversible step: the purge after 30 days.

Data: business-data-context flow-workspace-deletion, state-workspace.

Cross-feature flow: the traceability chain

No single feature owns the product's promise; five features hand it along and two reports read it back:

  1. Explorer: a user story with ordered acceptance criteria (journey-build-project-structure).
  2. ATC editor: the ATC is anchored to that story and bound to one or more of its criteria (journey-author-atc).
  3. Test builder: ATCs are chained by reference, so an ATC edit reaches every Test that uses it (journey-compose-test).
  4. Runner: a run freezes the chain and records per-step results (journey-execute-test-run).
  5. Bug dialog: a failed step becomes a bug that keeps links to the run, the step and the ATC (journey-file-and-triage-bug).
  6. Metrics and Traceability read the chain per criterion and per story (journey-review-quality).

Where it can break. Archiving a module removes its stories, criteria and ATCs from coverage while their Tests, runs and bugs remain; how a Test view and a run start treat an archived ATC inside a chain was not verified. Only 12 of 1,755 bugs in the shared database carry the run link, so the run-to-bug hop is rarely exercised.

Cross-feature flow: an ATC edit and the Tests and runs that use it

  • Saving an ATC bumps its version and answers with the number of Tests that chain it; the editor's preview shows usage (GET /api/v1/atcs/{id}/usage).
  • Every Test that chains the ATC shows the new steps on its next read: Tests hold references, not copies.
  • Runs already started keep their frozen copy; history never changes. A run started after the edit executes the new content.
  • Test impact: a single ATC edit changes several Tests at once without any action on those Tests, so a regression set can change between two runs of the same Test. The audit row atc.updated lists the affected Tests (Activity feed).

Data: business-data-context entity-atc, entity-run.

Cross-feature flow: notifications

  • Producers: Runs (finished or aborted, to the starter, unless the starter closed it from the browser) and Bugs (assignment to the new assignee; status change to reporter and assignee, never the actor). Nothing else notifies.
  • Inbox: the sidebar bell shows the unread count, a panel lists the last 90 days, rows arrive live; read one or "mark all read" (POST /api/v1/notifications/{id}/read, …/notifications/read-all).
  • Email: a daily digest at 08:00 UTC from production only (staging has no cron); its link opens the inbox through a query parameter (OpenInboxFromQuery).
  • Preferences: Settings, Notifications, a grid of run and bug lifecycle times in-app and email; only the email column changes behaviour.
  • Test impact: a notification test needs two accounts (actor and recipient) because self-actions are suppressed.

Data: business-data-context flow-notifications, entity-notification.

Cross-feature flow: the active workspace

  • Every signed-in page resolves one active workspace from a cookie (falling back to the user's first workspace) and scopes the sidebar's projects, the role shown in the account menu, the notification count and the settings navigation to it.
  • Project URLs carry only the project slug: /projects/{slug} is resolved inside the active workspace, so the same URL can mean a different project, or not found, after a switch.
  • Switching (POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace) refreshes the shell; role-dependent controls follow the new role.
  • Test impact: tenant isolation is tested by switching workspaces and by opening another workspace's ids directly; both must answer not found, never forbidden with data.

API endpoint inventory (pointer)

Endpoint groups belong to business-api-context, whose map is not generated yet (placeholder). Until it is, the contract is /api/openapi: 102 operations under 26 tags (Workspaces 15; Bugs and Runs 7 each; ATCs, Auth, Test Plans and Tests 6 each; Acceptance Criteria, Invites, Notifications and User Stories 5 each; Environments 4; Milestones, Modules and Tokens 3 each; Admin, Billing, Health, Identity and Imports 2 each; Activity, Coverage, Metrics, Projects, Search and Traceability 1 each). Each feature in this map names the endpoints its UI calls.

Test accounts needed

Declared: one user per environment (LOCAL_USER_EMAIL, STAGING_USER_EMAIL, with their passwords). Needed for the journeys above: one account per role (viewer, member, admin, owner) in a shared workspace, plus a second member for notification and assignment tests. Account creation is a team decision; none of these exist in .env.example.

Smoke scope suggestion

Sign in, open Home, open a project workbench, open a Test, start and abort a run on a seeded environment, open Bug Reports. Each step uses only member rights and no external dependency.

Discovery gaps

  • No browser session was run for this map (code, maps and read-only MCPs only): every journey is traced from code, and UI timing, layout and live-update behaviour are unverified.
  • The API map (business-api-context) is a placeholder, so the endpoint pointers in this map have no section ids to point to yet.
  • Members page /workspaces/{id}/members has no reachable link: its only link is in components/layout/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx, which no page renders; Settings lists Members as coming soon. Whether this is intended is a product question.
  • Viewers see "New ATC", "New Test" and the ATC editor's Save; the database refuses the write. The exact message a viewer gets on save was not verified.
  • Every project's explorer lists all Tests of the workspace, including Tests whose ATCs are in other projects; intended (Tests are workspace-scoped) or a display bug is not confirmed.
  • The browser ATC editor saves with no expected version (ifMatch: null); whether two people editing the same ATC can overwrite each other silently was not verified.
  • The message shown when the plan's project limit refuses a new project is not mapped in create-project-form.tsx; the user probably sees a generic error (not verified).
  • Password reset, profile edit, member role change and member removal: no route or form found. Not verified whether Supabase's hosted flows cover any of them.
  • Which role STAGING_USER_EMAIL holds, and in which workspace, was not verified (secret values are not read).
  • GitHub and Google OAuth provider configuration per environment, Stripe test mode on staging, and Resend delivery on staging: not verified.
  • How a Test view and a run start treat an archived ATC inside a chain: not verified (also in the data map gaps).
  • Domain map contradiction (built at e88512e): it says no Tests, Runs, bugs, dashboards or Jira sync exist and that plan tiers have no billing; current code has all of them. It also expands ATC as "Atomic Test Component"; current code says "Acceptance Test Case".
  • Infra map contradiction (e88512e): "no vercel.json, no cron, no workers" is outdated; there is a Vercel cron, two pg_cron jobs and three background workers.
  • /about is in Spanish while the app UI is English; the target audience of each public page was not confirmed.
  • Usage numbers come from a database shared by local, staging and production and filled mostly by automated tests; they show what is exercised, not customer behaviour.
  • No legacy persona, journey or functional-spec files exist (.context/PRD/, .context/SRS/, .context/business/ are absent), so nothing was migrated.
